title: India's Index of industrial production records growth of 6.7% in July 2026.
subtitle: Quick Estimates of Index of Industrial Production and Use- Based Index for the Month of July 2026 (Base 2022-23=100)
body_text:
In July 2026, Index of Industrial Production recorded a 6.7% year-on-year growth, supported by 7.3% growth in Manufacturing sector and strong growth of 8.7% in Electricity & Gas Supply sector.
The Quick Estimate of Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is released on 28 th of every month (or next working day if 28 th is a holiday). The index is compiled with data received from source agencies, which in turn receive the data from the producing factories/ establishments. These Quick Estimates will undergo revision in subsequent releases as per the revision policy of IIP.
2.  Key Highlights:
The IIP growth rate for the month of July 2026 is 6.7 percent which was 7.3 percent (Quick Estimate) in the month of June 2026. The growth rates of the sectors, Mining & Quarrying, Manufacturing, Electricity & Gas Supply and Water Supply, Sewerage & Waste Management for the month of July 2026 are (-) 0.9 percent, 7.3 percent, 8.7 percent and 7.4 percent respectively. The Quick Estimate of IIP stands at 124.8 against 117.0 in July 2025. The indices of Industrial Production for Mining & Quarrying, Manufacturing, Electricity & Gas Supply and Water Supply, Sewerage & Waste Management for the month of July 2026 stand at 94.4, 127.4, 133.5 and 148.4 respectively. Within the Manufacturing sector, 19 out of 23 industry groups at NIC 2 digit-level have recorded a positive growth in July 2026 over July 2025. The top three positive contributors for the month of July 2026 are – “Manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers” (22.2%), “Manufacture of electrical equipment” (28.3%), and “Manufacture of machinery and equipment n.e.c.” (12.1%). In the industry group “Manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers” item groups “Auto Components, Spares and Accessories”, “Passenger Cars”, and “Commercial Vehicles” have shown significant contribution in growth. In the industry group “Manufacture of electrical equipment”, item groups “Electrical Apparatus for Switching or Protecting Electrical Circuits (e.g., Switchgear, Circuit Breakers/Switches, Control/Meter Panels) and Parts Thereof”, “UPS and Solid-State Drives”, and “End-Face Connectors for Optical Fibres and Cables” have shown significant contribution in growth. In the industry group “Manufacture of machinery and equipment n.e.c.”, item groups “Construction Machinery/Equipment (Incl. Bulldozers and Road Rollers)”, “Pumps of All Types (Centrifugal, Hydraulic, Positive Displacement, Gear, Screw, Gravity, Steam, Boiler Feed, Valveless Pumps, etc.)”, and “Steam/Vapour, Wind and Other Turbines” have shown significant contribution in growth. As per the Use-Based Classification, the indices stand at 115.9 for Primary Goods, 141.8 for Capital Goods, 130.9 for Intermediate Goods and 136.2 for Infrastructure/ Construction Goods for the month of July 2026. Further, the indices for Consumer durables and Consumer non-durables stand at 129.9 and 113.7 respectively. The corresponding growth rates of IIP as per Use-Based Classification in July 2026 over July 2025 are 4.1 percent in Primary Goods, 16.1 percent in Capital Goods, 10.0 percent in Intermediate Goods, 6.9 percent in Infrastructure/ Construction Goods, 10.5 percent in Consumer durables and (-)1.0 percent in Consumer non-durables (Statement III).  Based on Use-Based Classification, top three positive contributors to the growth of IIP for the month of July 2026 are Intermediate Goods, Capital Goods and Primary goods.
Along with the Quick Estimate of IIP for the month of July 2026, the indices for June 2026 have undergone final revision in the light of the updated data received from the source agencies. The Quick Estimates for July 2026 and the final revision for June 2026 have been compiled at weighted response rates of 88.9 percent and 93.0 percent respectively. Details of Quick Estimates of the Index of Industrial Production for the month of July 2026 at Sector, Sub-Sector, 2-digit level of National Industrial Classification (NIC-2025), by Use-Based Classification and are given at Statements I, II (A, B, C, D) and III respectively. Also, for users to appreciate the changes in the industrial sector, Statement IV provides month-wise indices for the last 13 months, by industry groups (as per 2-digit level of NIC-2025), sectors and Sub-Sectors. Release of the IIP for August 2026 will be on Monday, 28th September 2026.
Note: -
This Press Release (English and Hindi Version) is also available at the Ministry’s Website - http://www.mospi.gov.in . Detailed data pertaining to IIP is available at https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/macroindicators?product=iip

enrichment.summary: India's Index of Industrial Production (IIP) grew 6.7% year-on-year in July 2026, driven by 7.3% growth in manufacturing and 8.7% growth in Electricity & Gas Supply, though this was slower than June 2026's 7.3% growth. Mining & Quarrying contracted by 0.9%, while 19 of 23 manufacturing industry groups posted positive growth, led by electrical equipment (28.3%), motor vehicles (22.2%), and machinery (12.1%). Under Use-Based Classification, Capital Goods (16.1%) and Intermediate Goods (10.0%) led growth, while Consumer Non-durables contracted by 1.0%.
enrichment.context:
The IIP is a key monthly high-frequency indicator compiled by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), tracking short-term changes in industrial output across mining, manufacturing, and electricity sectors. It is released as a 'Quick Estimate' on the 28th of each month with subsequent revisions, and serves as a proxy for industrial-sector momentum feeding into GDP estimation and monetary policy decisions by the RBI. The base year was recently updated to 2022-23=100, aligning with NIC-2025 classification, reflecting periodic methodological updates to keep the index representative of the current industrial structure.

The divergence between strong capital goods growth (16.1%) and consumer non-durables contraction (-1.0%) is analytically significant: capital goods growth typically signals investment activity and future productive capacity expansion, while weak consumer non-durables (like FMCG) growth can indicate softer rural or mass-market consumption demand. Similarly, the sharp contraction in mining (-0.9%) alongside robust electricity growth (8.7%) reflects sector-specific dynamics that aggregate indices can mask. Such monthly releases are part of India's broader statistical ecosystem including CPI, WPI, and GDP estimates, which collectively inform fiscal and monetary policy calibration.

prelims_questions.question: The Index of Industrial Production (IIP) released by the National Statistical Office is currently based on which base year?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, the IIP is currently compiled with Base 2022-23=100, following a revision from the earlier base year.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following sectors is NOT one of the four sectors covered under the sectoral classification of India's IIP?
prelims_questions.explanation: The IIP's sectoral classification covers Mining & Quarrying, Manufacturing, Electricity & Gas Supply, and Water Supply, Sewerage & Waste Management; Construction is not a separate IIP sector, though 'Infrastructure/Construction Goods' appears under Use-Based Classification.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of the Index of Industrial Production (IIP) as a high-frequency economic indicator. What are its limitations in capturing the true state of India's industrial economy?

Analyze the divergent growth trends across Use-Based Classification categories (Capital Goods vs. Consumer Non-durables) in recent IIP data and discuss what this reveals about the current state of investment and consumption demand in the Indian economy.

study_notes.reason: This is a routine monthly statistical release; its value lies almost entirely in facts (index compiler, base year, growth figures, sectoral classification) rather than sustained analytical argument, though the capital-goods vs consumer-non-durables divergence offers a modest analytical hook.

prelims.point: IIP is compiled by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), released as a 'Quick Estimate' on the 28th of every month
prelims.why_important: Tests knowledge of the compiling agency and release schedule of a key high-frequency indicator, a recurring UPSC theme on economic statistics.

prelims.point: IIP base year has been updated to 2022-23=100, aligned with NIC-2025 classification
prelims.why_important: Base year revisions of major indices (IIP, CPI, WPI) are a classic prelims distractor point testing awareness of current methodology.

prelims.point: IIP covers three broad sectors — Mining & Quarrying, Manufacturing, and Electricity & Gas Supply — with Manufacturing having the highest weight (76.062%)
prelims.why_important: UPSC often tests sectoral weights/composition of indices to check whether candidates confuse IIP's sectoral coverage with GDP sectoral shares.

prelims.point: Under Use-Based Classification, IIP items are grouped into Primary Goods, Capital Goods, Intermediate Goods, Infrastructure/Construction Goods, Consumer Durables and Consumer Non-durables
prelims.why_important: Distinguishing IIP's sectoral classification from its use-based classification is a common source of confusion in objective questions.

prelims.point: In July 2026, Mining & Quarrying contracted by 0.9% while Electricity & Gas Supply grew 8.7% and Manufacturing grew 7.3%, giving overall IIP growth of 6.7%
prelims.why_important: Specific sector-wise growth figures for the latest release could appear in a current-affairs based prelims question on economic indicators.

mains.point: Divergence between strong Capital Goods growth (16.1%) and contraction in Consumer Non-durables (-1.0%) signals robust investment activity alongside weak mass-market/rural consumption demand
mains.analytical_use: Useful for analysing questions on the health of India's investment cycle versus consumption demand, and what such divergence implies for growth sustainability.

mains.point: Contraction in Mining & Quarrying (-0.9%) despite robust Electricity growth (8.7%) shows aggregate indices can mask sector-specific weaknesses
mains.analytical_use: Can be used in answers examining the limitations of composite indices like IIP in capturing sub-sectoral distress, relevant to questions on data reliability.

mains.point: IIP serves as a proxy for industrial-sector momentum feeding into GDP estimation and RBI's monetary policy calibration
mains.theme: Role of high-frequency indicators in policy
mains.analytical_use: Supports answers on how high-frequency data informs fiscal/monetary policy-making and the importance of timely statistics for macroeconomic management.

low_priority.reason: Too granular sub-item detail with no standalone examinable or analytical value beyond illustrating already-noted sector growth.

low_priority.reason: Methodological administrative detail without significance for either factual recall or analysis.

related_articles.relationship: The Index of Core Industries (ICI) tracks eight core sectors (including mining, electricity, and steel) that are key inputs into the IIP calculation, and both releases cover the same July 2026 reference month with comparable growth trends in electricity and contraction in some heavy industries.
